sources.fullCitation: Stare Melodie. “Może tak, może nie.” Polish-language song entry with words by Julian Tuwim and a recording by Zofia Terné, Columbia DM 1624 a, matrix WJ 277, 1932; linked on the page to “Gib nur acht, über Nacht kommt die Liebe.”
sources.title: Może tak, może nie — Columbia DM 1624 a
sources.creator: Stare Melodie
sources.researchNote: The page groups Fritz Rotter and Bronisław Kaper under music. The work-level credits follow contemporary German registrations, which assign the music to Kaper and the German words to Rotter.

sources.shortCitation: Syrena Grand Record 17921, “A zresztą… niech pan zadzwoni” (1926)
sources.fullCitation: Orkiestra teatru „Perskie Oko”, conducted by Z. Wiehler. “A zresztą… niech pan zadzwoni.” Shimmy. Syrena Grand Record, no. 17921. Transfer from a privately held disc published by Stare Melodie on YouTube, 10 April 2025.
sources.title: A zresztą… niech pan zadzwoni — Syrena Grand Record 17921
sources.creator: Orkiestra teatru „Perskie Oko”; Zygmunt Wiehler, conductor
sources.researchNote: The displayed label confirms the title, orchestra, conductor Z. Wiehler and number 17921. The uploader reports 1926 and calls 17921 the matrix as well as the disc number; the label image alone does not establish a separate matrix number. KPPG record 38213 independently dates the coupled 17919/17921 disc to 1926. The upload description credits Henryk Chwast under the pseudonym Bruno Asper; both forms are independently documented as Kaper’s pseudonyms.

additionalLinks.label: KPPG record 38213 — coupled Syrena sides 17919 and 17921

sources.shortCitation: Stare Melodie, “O tym już wróble świergocą na dachu” — Syrena-Electro 3461 (1930)
sources.fullCitation: Stare Melodie. “O tym już wróble świergocą na dachu.” Tadeusz Faliszewski with the orchestra of Towarzystwo Syrena Record; recording dated March 1930 in the listening-entry metadata. Syrena-Electro 3461, matrix 20876.
sources.title: O tym już wróble świergocą na dachu — Syrena-Electro 3461
sources.creator: Stare Melodie
sources.researchNote: The Stare Melodie listening entry dates the recording to March 1930. An embedded YouTube title instead gives 1929; the site’s editor explicitly corrects that year to March 1930 in the comments. The structured date follows the site’s catalogue entry and identifies the recording, not a separately established issue date.
